core: No SQLite. The three JSON docs ARE the data layer; app loads them at startup and renders reference cards
upside: Zero migration cost; evidence stays canonical and diffable; fastest to hackathon
risk: No join surface for live telemetry; every query is an in-memory scan; user has already decided SQLite
test: Load the 3 files in the app and render one crop card; time it

core: SQLite as operational join layer only; evidence documents stored verbatim as JSON blobs plus typed projections; measurement + deployment + evaluation tables around them
upside: Live telemetry joins to evidence without remodelling claims; claim_role/prohibited_use survive; admission policy is one UPDATE
risk: More build cost than O1; projections can drift from the blob if not derived at load
test: Load the 3 docs, assert projection row counts equal record counts (13 + 17)

core: SQLite with universal per-crop min/max normal ranges per axis and a composite 0-100 score
upside: Simple UI; matches the original request literally
risk: Fabricates a response surface never measured; violates prohibited_use on every record; 3 of 8 crops have zero data; RH growth optimum exists for no crop
test: Try to write the basil RH normal-range row from the corpus; observe it cannot be sourced

core: Trial-grid representation: store the tested treatment levels themselves; place the live reading on the literal experimental grid
upside: Cannot imply an unmeasured response shape; honest about grid spacing and unbounded ends
risk: Users may still read spatial proximity as an implicit grade; 2D factorials (coriander PPFD x photoperiod) are awkward to render
test: Render basil temp strip 11|17|23|[29]|35 with a live reading and show it to a non-author

core: Claim-typed evaluation panels: growth_evidence, disease_conditions, human_air_quality, site_noise_standard — never composed
upside: Prevents the growth+health+law category error; unknown/blocked are first-class; matches record semantics exactly
risk: Four panels is more UI than a single number; operator may still want one number
test: Write the four panel contracts and check each of the 13 records maps to exactly one
